description:
Nobody in this book commits a crime. Elena Richardson follows every rule, means well the entire time — and still burns three lives to the ground.

That's the core of Little Fires Everywhere by Celeste Ng — and this deep dive argues one idea: the real danger in a community isn't the rule-breaker, it's the well-meaning rule-follower who mistakes her own comfort for justice. We trace it through Shaker Heights' obsessive order, two colliding theories of motherhood, a custody trial where the 'reasonable' verdict is the cruel one, Elena's surveillance disguised as care, a teenage daughter who turns out to be the family's only conscience, and an ending that refuses to let anyone off the hook.
